problem.title: Five Friends in a Row
problem.statement: Ava, Ben, Chen, Dia, and Eli will stand in five numbered positions from left to right. Each friend occupies exactly one position. How many different lineups are possible?
hints: Choose who stands first, then update the pool of people still available.
How many choices remain for the second position after the first is filled?

solutionSteps.title: Fill the first two positions
solutionSteps.body: Any of 5 friends can stand first. After that person is used, 4 friends remain for second.

solutionSteps.title: Continue the shrinking choices
solutionSteps.body: The last three positions have 3, then 2, then 1 remaining choice.

solutionSteps.title: Multiply successive choices
solutionSteps.body: Every finished lineup follows exactly one branch, so 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 lineups.

validationMethods: independent recursive enumeration into five first-person groups of 24 suffix orders
notes: Both the grouped enumeration and shrinking-position product give 120.

problem.title: Six Books on a Shelf
problem.statement: Six distinct books are placed in a row on a shelf. How many different left-to-right arrangements are possible?
hints: The books are distinct and every shelf position matters.
How many choices remain after one book is placed?

solutionSteps.title: Fill the shelf
solutionSteps.body: The six positions have 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 choices in order.

solutionSteps.title: Use factorial notation
solutionSteps.body: Thus the number of arrangements is 6! = 6 × 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 720.

validationMethods: recursive arrangement count 6×(number of five-book arrangements)=6×120
notes: The recursive count and direct factorial evaluation both give 720.

problem.title: Three Medals
problem.statement: Five finalists compete for gold, silver, and bronze medals. No finalist can win more than one medal. How many different medal assignments are possible?
hints: Gold, silver, and bronze are different roles.
The shrinking product stops after the third medal is assigned.

solutionSteps.title: Assign gold
solutionSteps.body: Any of the 5 finalists can win gold.

solutionSteps.title: Assign the remaining medals
solutionSteps.body: There are 4 remaining choices for silver and then 3 for bronze.

solutionSteps.title: Multiply
solutionSteps.body: The number of medal assignments is 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.

validationMethods: independent choose-then-order check: 10 finalist triples, each with 6 medal orders
notes: Both methods give 60, and the product correctly stops after three roles.

problem.title: Four Signal Flags
problem.statement: Four flags are placed in a row. Two flags are identical red flags, one is blue, and one is green. How many visibly different color arrangements are possible?
hints: Choose a position for blue and then a different position for green.
Once blue and green are placed, do the identical red flags create another visible choice?

solutionSteps.title: Place blue
solutionSteps.body: The blue flag has 4 possible positions.

solutionSteps.title: Place green
solutionSteps.body: After blue is placed, green has 3 possible positions.

solutionSteps.title: Fill with red
solutionSteps.body: The two remaining positions both receive identical red flags, so there is only one visible completion. Thus 4 × 3 × 1 = 12.

validationMethods: direct placement count using 4 blue positions and 3 remaining green positions
notes: Both methods give 12; swapping the red flags never changes the visible outcome.

problem.title: Committee of Three
problem.statement: Ava, Ben, Chen, and Dia will choose a three-person committee. The committee has no special roles. How many different committees are possible?
hints: Changing the order of the same three names does not create a new committee.
Each committee can be identified by the one person who sits out.

solutionSteps.title: Describe an outcome once
solutionSteps.body: A three-person committee from four people is determined by the one person not chosen.

solutionSteps.title: List the disjoint cases
solutionSteps.body: Ava, Ben, Chen, or Dia can be the person who sits out, giving 4 committees.

solutionSteps.title: Check order
solutionSteps.body: Reordering the three chosen names does not change membership, so those name orders must not be counted again.

validationMethods: exhaustive list of the four committees ABC, ABD, ACD, and BCD
independent bijection with the four possible omitted people
notes: Both independent descriptions give 4 committees and count each membership set once.

problem.title: Artifacts at the Ends
problem.statement: Six distinct artifacts are arranged in a row. The Sun artifact and the Moon artifact must occupy the two end positions, in either order. How many arrangements are possible?
hints: First count the possible left-right orders of Sun and Moon on the ends.
For each end order, arrange the other four distinct artifacts in the middle.

solutionSteps.title: Fill the ends
solutionSteps.body: Sun and Moon can occupy the left and right ends in 2 orders.

solutionSteps.title: Fill the middle
solutionSteps.body: For each end order, the other four distinct artifacts can fill the middle in 4! = 24 ways.

validationMethods: two disjoint end-order cases with 24 middle permutations in each
independent position-first calculation 2 choices for the left special artifact followed by 4! middle orders
notes: Both counts give 2×4!=48, and the two end orders are disjoint.
